overview.title: Game Mechanics Overview
overview.description: Expanse EDU transforms education into an engaging game experience through proven game design principles. The platform incorporates progression systems, rewards, competition, and social features to motivate students while teaching valuable life skills.
overview.corePhilosophy: Generally speaking ONE of the highest values we can create and offer for students and teachers is from money and things that come from money. This system is meant to be reflective of the real world and additionally help teach the value of money and managing resources.

keyPillars.name: Progression & Leveling
keyPillars.description: Users gain experience by completing tasks, level up, and earn unlockable content and features

keyPillars.name: Rewards & Incentives
keyPillars.description: A variety of rewards received and purchasable for Students and Teachers from multiple sources

keyPillars.name: Competition & Battles
keyPillars.description: Healthy competition drives performance through PvP battles, team competitions, and rankings

keyPillars.name: Customization & Expression
keyPillars.description: Personalization through equipment, items, avatars, and collectibles

keyPillars.name: Social & Recognition
keyPillars.description: Peer recognition, achievements, and social features build community

currencies.title: Currency System
currencies.description: Coins and gems are earned from task completion and other aspects of the system such as participation, acknowledgement, battles, etc. These are then used in stores to obtain a variety of rewards.

types.name: Coins
types.purpose: Primary currency for purchasing rewards and items

types.name: Gems
types.purpose: Premium currency for special purchases and features
types.notes: Could charge money for special gem types

types.name: Lottery Tickets
types.purpose: Chance-based rewards for scholarships and special items
types.acquisition: Coins/gems can purchase lottery tickets towards specific things

progression.title: Progression & Leveling System
progression.description: Students earn experience as they complete rewardable activities and battles. Progress bars with checkpoints similar to Starbucks or Panera with completion rewards.

progressionTypes.description: Overall experience earned contributing to a level
Leveling up problem solving skills by taking math, etc.
Science, math, english etc. Gain experience in specific categories
progressionTypes.concerns: Classification of courses, missing data from previous years

progressionTypes.description: Points at which a user will evolve into a new level that unlocks additional abilities, content, perks, etc.
Milestone-based progression with specific completion requirements

progression.groupProgression: The more students in the classroom/school that submit assignments the more experience the group earns
designNotes: Iterative release schedule with gradual improvements
Perhaps 60/40% experience gain - 40% at end, 60% throughout class
Quarterly release of experience amounts in higher quantities
Likely needs to be time based
Set a certain amount to be the goal amount to be gained for each class
risks: May not be able to trust assignments listed in the system - time based disbursement may help

quests.title: Quest System
quests.description: Users complete quests for different activities in the system or classrooms. Quests provide additional rewards, experience, or perks.
purposes: Get students to give feedback to teachers
Use different features in the application
Remove awkward barriers by instructing students to socialize/request feedback

teachers: Setup stores and custom rewards for classroom
Put up visual recognition of top performers
schools: Put up visual recognition throughout school
Setup school reward offerings (Movie day, Field Trips, Cookie days, Free Popcorn, etc)

quests.value: Product exploration, goals, guidance, positive reinforcement

achievements.title: Achievement System
achievements.description: An achievement is a form of accomplishment celebration and high level goal. Students earn achievements by completing various predefined requirements.
examples: Earn > 90% on 5 assignments in a row
achievements.value: Positive reinforcement and guide mechanic that can increase performance in school, mental health, and app usage. Also serves as guidance.

battles.title: Battles & Competition
battles.philosophy: People love battles and competition. Sports are popular for a reason. People love watching the best of the best, and people love winning. Competition drives people to perform their best. Games are the epitome of engagement.
battles.vision: Turn school into a game in a healthy way to improve outcomes for students worldwide.

battleTypes.description: Individual students within same class and between similar classes matched against each other
battleTypes.basis: Who gets the higher grade or completion % on assignments and tests

battleTypes.description: Compare classes by period (1st period vs 2nd period vs 7th period)
Choose your teammates (3-5 players), compete against other teams
School-wide competition, likely based on completion % rather than grades
Battle bosses and monsters based on grades, submissions, recognition
Completion activities and grades used to battle bosses collectively
Groups team up to battle monsters and bosses, explore dungeons

combatMechanics.dps: Attendance, teacher feedback, check-ins contribute to damage
combatMechanics.aiCombat: Customize characters pre-emptively, select abilities used and played by AI. Students set up characters as specific roles and watch as AI plays based on selections.
combatMechanics.powerUps: Gain boosts from applying buffs beforehand (check ins)
combatMechanics.replays: Allow replay watching of battles to see how they turned out

tournaments.description: Large regularly scheduled tournaments with different rewards such as scholarships
tournaments.format: Play many different rounds for better sorting, only highlight top winners

rankings.system: ELO rating system where students are sorted based on wins and losses
features: Individual performance tracking within team battles

mentalHealthConsiderations: Highlight winners, work as a team
Assign teams to mix strong and weaker performers so weaker performers get recognized too
Real names not shown - use usernames or generated names until picked
Team-based recognition instead of just individuals
risks: Players intentionally doing poorly to sabotage teammates or fear of judgement
Can prevent showing team members, eliminate people for not participating
Competition & Anger/Frustration - Can be addicting but good for developing risk tolerance

personalization.title: Game Personalization & Customization
personalization.description: Collect rare items and become stronger with the ability to customize preferred areas. Students can redeem equipment and consumable items that incorporate a rarity system.

categories.name: Equipment & Items
categories.description: Collect rare items and become stronger with ability to customize preferred areas

categories.name: Buffs & Consumables
categories.description: Temporary powerups to boost experience, battle performance, goal progression, coins, etc.

categories.name: Skills
categories.description: May be related to class/subjects and education

categories.name: Talents
categories.description: May be related to class/subjects and education

categories.name: Profile Display
categories.description: User profiles for students, teachers, classrooms, schools

categories.name: Art & NFTs
categories.description: Art can become NFT artwork with unique IDs, transferable to digital wallets. Each piece can be one of a kind using AI image generation.

categories.name: AI Flows
categories.description: Setup how a battle will play out and what moves the AI will take. Teach people how to use AI through the game.

categories.name: Perks
categories.description: Badges or gear that include special perks as power-ups granting bonus rewards
categories.mechanics: Only a certain number of perks can be utilized at the same time
examplePerks: 1% additional chance at second loot box on assignment completion

categories.name: Specializations
categories.description: May be related to class/subjects and education

categories.name: Color Theme
categories.description: Users can choose their color theme for the application (Blue, Red, Purple, etc.). Represents Expanse's philosophy of choice, personalization, and self-determination.

raritySystem.description: Reward rarities have associated colors with them. Higher rarity often have higher levels of benefit.

collectibles.description: Items will be collectible, sets of unique item types

profiles.title: Profile System
profiles.description: Comprehensive profile system for users, classrooms, and schools with customization options.

userProfiles.description: User profiles with customizable public display levels
userProfiles.value: Auxiliary/personalization, supporting feature, required for scale

schoolProfiles.description: School profiles where schools can advertise information and have specific rewards/stores
features: Display statistics (attendance, growth metrics, XP earned, rewards purchased/redeemed, parent involvement)
Display students by avatars and usernames (not real names)

stores.title: Stores & Store Setup
stores.description: Users can set up stores with custom rewards for students or teachers to purchase.
ideas: Teachers as NPCs with game reward options so they have additional options without spending personal funds

rewards.title: Reward System
rewards.description: A comprehensive system for earning, tracking, and redeeming various types of rewards.
rewards.lootBoxes: Receive loot boxes that include artwork, gems, and perks by submitting assignments and attending class

experiences: School Events (Free Snacks, Game tickets, Movie in Auditorium)
Movie Nights, Bowling Trips, Ice cream/Cookie party
recognition: Visual recognition on screens in hallways

visualStimulation: Characters celebrating achievements (happy face, geometric shaped characters)

rankings.title: Rankings & Performance
rankings.description: See where you rank on homework assignments or tests. Did you rank in the top 10%? How do your grades compare?

leaderboards.description: Would be configurable. Show top X number of students for experience/grades/attendance
features: Divided into groups (random or similar schools by funding/diversity)

rankings.concerns: Actual data display may not be good for low performers - should be configurable

recognition.title: Feedback, Recognition & Acknowledgement
recognition.description: Systems for recognizing students and teachers for doing good work, with associated rewards and social announcements.

recognitionTypes.description: Time-based requests for feedback with notifications
recognitionTypes.feature: Students can request recognition from teachers

recognitionTypes.description: Anonymous feedback to teacher or about classroom
recognitionTypes.feature: Feedback to school/district if teachers not meeting expectations
Send thumbs up/congratulations to other students

recognitionTypes.description: Recognition of completed activities through chat integrations, social sharing, in-app displays

certificates: Earn different levels of certificates from Expanse based on performance
Recognition of achievement, effort, and graduation
futureIdeas: QR Code on desk to bring up recognition screen with student name selected

goals.title: Goals System
goals.description: Goals are either repeatable, one-time completion, interval, or a set number of times. Earn experience collectively towards goals and rewards.
examples: Work towards classroom rewards through attendance and submissions
Pizza day, fieldtrip, movie day, activities
goals.notes: Students having specific goals they are aiming to achieve helps motivate more than having no goals. Clear and specific goals are most effective.

social.title: Social Features
social.description: Social aspects are definitely really important. May require coins/gems to send chat messages.

features.name: Chatrooms
features.description: Talk to your classroom, communicate with teacher
considerations: May wait on announcements due to existing areas
Existing tools may not be as open for communication

features.name: Social Media Platform
features.description: School-wide social platform connecting all students
features: Content moderation (no violence, sex, theft topics)
AI image conversion for uploads (photos → illustrations)

features.name: Social Sharing
features.description: Share achievements to connected social profiles
features: Scholarship redemption shared publicly by default

social.socialSharing: Scholarship redemption will likely be shared publicly by default

userJourneys.title: User Journeys

coreFlow.title: Core Starter Product Flow
highLevel: Reward Coins, Loot, and Enable Other Features
details: Event activity is identified from monitoring changes in LMS data
Rewardable events are noted and tracked by Expanse
Student reviews activity in Expanse EDU
Student redeems rewards for rewardable event activity
Student receives: rewards, recognition, and digital currency

parentOnboarding: Students invite parents to the application
Parents create an account and add information
Parents add payment information and pay monthly fee and/or upfront amount
Payment goes to students for homework completion with good grades
Parent configures distribution timing and amounts
Parents choose which reward types their student can receive

expansions.title: Expansions & Seasons
expansions.description: Release expansions that unlock additional NFTs, gear, loot, spells, talents, battle types, features, etc.

seasons.description: Ranking, competition, leaderboard features will have reset periods where ratings reset or reduce
seasons.purpose: Give a chance for newcomers to take the top of the leaderboards

expansions.seasonalRewards: Some rewards may only be offered on holidays or for limited time events

lmsIntegration.title: LMS/SIS Event Detection
lmsIntegration.description: When a change occurs in the LMS we can compare old data to new data to identify if a change event has occurred.
process: Detect changes in LMS data (e.g., submissions)
Mark assignment as rewarded or not
If not yet rewarded, make eligible for rewards
After rewards given, mark as rewarded

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: Many features will be configurable and toggle-able on various levels.

negativeReinforcement.title: Negative Reinforcement & Consequences
negativeReinforcement.description: Balanced consequences for poor performance or behavior, designed to motivate improvement without being punitive.
negativeReinforcement.philosophy: Consequences should be proportional, transparent, and focused on encouraging positive change rather than punishment.

consequenceTypes.description: Small deductions from earned currency for specific behaviors
Limited access to stores or rewards for a set period
Fewer available choices in customization or rewards
Reduced contribution toward classroom or school goals
Lower loot box rewards or XP multipliers
Temporary stat reductions in competitive modes

implementation: Consequences are configurable by teachers and administrators
Students always understand why consequences were applied
Clear path to remove consequences through positive behavior
Never impacts core learning or essential features
risks: Must be carefully balanced with positive reinforcement
Requires clear communication of rules upfront

historyReflection.title: History & Reflection
historyReflection.description: Systems for reviewing past performance, celebrating accomplishments, and reflecting on progress over time.
features: Look back at experience earned over the year

visualizations.description: Visual graphs showing progress over time
Detailed event logs and activity history
Chronological view of achievements and milestones

historyReflection.value: Helps students see their growth, reinforces positive behaviors, and provides data for goal-setting
historyReflection.privacyNote: Grade/ranking insights are optional and configurable to protect low performers

games.title: Games & Mini-Games
games.description: Various game modes and mini-games that enhance engagement and provide alternative ways to earn rewards.

gameTypes.description: Quick educational games tied to subjects
Games leveraging AI for dynamic gameplay

games.value: Increases engagement variety and provides alternative reward paths
